title: Adrenochrome: From Fiction to QAnon
summary: Origin chain of the elite baby-eating/adrenochrome claim: Hunter S. Thompson's 1971 FICTION 'Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas' → Gilliam's 1998 film → 4chan /x/ (2013) and /pol/ (2014) → Pizzagate (2016) → QAnon (2017+). Scientific reality: adrenochrome is a real chemical (oxidized adrenaline) — unstable, no fountain-of-youth properties, synthesized industrially. NO primary source — no court filing, FBI file, testimony or DOJ release — connects Epstein or any public figure to adrenochrome harvesting or ritual sacrifice.
tldr: The claim that elites harvest children's blood for adrenochrome traces back to Hunter S. Thompson's 1971 fiction 'Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas,' not to any real evidence — and the chemical itself is readily synthesized in labs, no human sacrifice required.
ai_summary:
AI review of the McGill Office for Science and Society article "QAnon's Adrenochrome Quackery" (Joe Schwarcz, Feb 10, 2022), read in full:
- Origin seed: Thompson's 1971 novel describes adrenochrome as "making pure mescaline seem like ginger beer" and claims "There's only one source for this stuff, the adrenalin glands from a living human body." The article says this fiction "likely planted the seed" of the conspiracy.
- Scientific backstory: Canadian psychiatrists Abram Hoffer and Humphry Osmond noted in the 1950s that adrenaline, when oxidized in the lab, forms adrenochrome (named from Greek "chroma" for its dark violet hue); their self-experiments led to the "Adrenochrome Hypothesis of Schizophrenia" — which collapsed when follow-up studies "failed to confirm any benefit."
- Pop-culture chain: the 1998 Terry Gilliam film adaptation carried adrenochrome into the movie, then a "totally forgettable" 2017 film titled "Adrenochrome" — setting the stage for QAnon's "perverse fabricated tale" of a Democratic-Hollywood pedophile ring harvesting blood.
- Reality check — verbatim: "Adrenochrome can be readily synthesized and is available to researchers from chemical suppliers. No need for human sacrifice." It has "no rejuvenating effects, and very questionable psychedelic properties."
- Harm: the article notes the belief has antisemitic blood-libel overtones and inspired a gunman who stormed a Washington pizza parlor hunting children he believed were held captive — sentenced to 4.5 years.
- Summary check: the Thompson→film→QAnon origin chain and the synthesized-chemical reality check are verified. Not verifiable from this source: the summary's 4chan /x/ (2013), /pol/ (2014), and Pizzagate (2016) intermediate steps, and any mention of Epstein — neither appears in the article.
